Why professional buyers look to Uruguay.
A small country with an outsized position in agricultural exports: a pastoral farming system, an industrial base that processes at origin, and export institutions that European buyers can verify.

Kunz Sourcing does not farm, process or slaughter itself. We work with established Uruguayan mills, plants and producers and put our name on the coordination: supplier selection, validation, documentation and export.
Sheep and cattle graze natural pasture in a temperate climate. Wool and beef here are products of extensive farming, not of sheds and feedlots.
Uruguay is one of the world's leading exporters of wool tops, and its beef plants are inspected by the Ministry of Livestock and listed for the markets they serve, including the EU.
IWTO-licensed laboratories test wool lots for yield, fibre diameter, vegetable matter and length. Cattle are individually identified in the national traceability system.
An investment-grade economy with stable institutions and regular container services from Montevideo to Northern Europe and the Mediterranean.
Two product areas from one origin.

Kunz Sourcing is a sourcing unit for Uruguayan export products, not a single-product trader. Wool is the most developed area today; beef enquiries are handled with EU-approved plants; further categories follow on request.

Grass, traceability and a sector built for export.
Uruguay exports most of the beef it produces, and the systems behind that trade are public: national traceability, ministry-inspected plants and a recognised animal-health status.

Kunz Sourcing is not a slaughterhouse and not the exporter of record. Beef is exported by EU-approved plants under their veterinary certification; we source, specify, check documentation and coordinate the commercial side for the buyer.
Cattle graze natural grassland year-round in a temperate climate. The use of hormonal growth promoters is prohibited in Uruguay.
Every bovine carries an individual identification and is registered in the national livestock traceability system (SNIG) from farm to slaughter.
Export plants are inspected by the Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries (MGAP) and listed for the markets they serve, including the European Union.
Uruguay holds WOAH-recognised status as free of foot-and-mouth disease with vaccination, the basis for its access to demanding markets.
Statements about feeding, animal health, residues and certifications are made only on the basis of the supplying plant's documentation for the specific product and lot.
